value.title: CORS Misconfiguration & Trust Verification Methodology
value.content: {"id": "portswigger_cors", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "cors", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)", "name": "CORS Misconfiguration & Trust Verification Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-942", "owasp_category": "A01:2021 - Broken Access Control", "signals": ["origin_reflection_in_acao", "wildcard_acao_with_credentials", "null_origin_trusted", "prefix_suffix_origin_trust", "intranet_origin_trust"], "verification_strategy": "Send HTTP requests containing arbitrary Origin headers (e.g. Origin: https://evil.com, Origin: null, Origin: https://example.com.attacker.com) with Access-Control-Request-Method, and observe Access-Control-Allow-Origin (ACAO) and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials (ACAC).", "evidence_requirements": ["arbitrary_acao_header", "acac_true_flag", "sensitive_api_response_body"], "tools": [{"tool": "httpx", "cmd": "httpx -u url -H 'Origin: https://attacker.com' -probe-headers 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin,Access-Control-Allow-Credentials'", "desc": "Differential header probing testing origin reflection"}, {"tool": "corsy", "cmd": "corsy -u url -d 1", "desc": "Automated CORS misconfiguration scanner validating reflection and null origin"}], "remediation": "Never reflect arbitrary Origin headers. Maintain an explicit allowlist of authorized origin domains. Avoid Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null and do not set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with wildcards.", "description": "PortSwigger CORS labs illustrate insecure CORS configurations where applications reflect arbitrary origins, trust null origins generated by sandboxed iframes, or utilize flawed regex matching susceptible to subdomain or prefix bypasses."}
